reasoning: Failure-driven edits are kept and take priority. Changes to them: (1) Step 0 is trimmed to a short mandatory type-check and archive-check line at the top, as the optimizer memory asks. It also keeps the one-line reasoning requirement. (2) The ECHO CHECK drops its foreign-word case, because Rule 1 already has the 'lambi -> Conch' bullet. Only the possessive/pronoun case and the altered-title case remain. (3) Concrete examples that may be gold answers or facts of specific training tasks ('Peru', 'Lincoln', 'Lyndon Johnson', 'sheep or goat') are replaced with placeholders, per the memory rule against embedding task facts. (4) The person-name default keeps its explicit tie-breakers: archive answers win, conventional initials stay, and the knight rule is untouched. Nothing weakens Rule 3. The bare-surname edit reinforces it. Success-driven edits are kept only where they cover patterns the failure edits do not: direction check for name clues, extra archive layouts (which supports Rule 3), the '...' alias-name fragment, series-level answers, and definition+etymology headwords. Their task-specific examples (Welsh, Decoration Day, yokel/barrel) are removed or generalized, and the text is shortened to limit growth in an already long skill. No edit targets text inside the SLOW_UPDATE markers. support_count and source_type are carried forward unchanged.

edits.content:
## Step 0 (mandatory: one reasoning line before every answer)
Write: `ARCHIVE = <quoted passage line where the clue is followed by an answer, or none>; SLOT = <person / thing / place / word>; ANSWER = <bare entity of that slot type>`.
- If ARCHIVE has a hit, copy that answer as printed (Rule 3). Otherwise reject any candidate that is not of the SLOT type or that the clue already states. 'He / she / who / this <role>' means a person's name, never a work named in the clue. 'Its <property> ...' means the bare noun that owns the property, not the property.

edits.target: - Ask: what category is the answer (country, person, vitamin, object, band), and what member of that category fits all the clue details?
edits.content:
- ECHO CHECK: the answer is never the clue's own subject or one of its own words.
  * A bare possessive or pronoun ('his final defeat', 'her debut', 'whose') after a named treaty, battle, work or event asks for the PERSON the pronoun refers to. The treaty or event is the anchor, not the answer.
  * Altered-title clues ('changed X to Y in this title', 'a parody of this title') ask for the ORIGINAL title with the changed word reversed, in its normal punctuation. Passages mostly show the parody form; do not copy it.

edits.target: If the list is of real people, answer with the team, state or other entity they share.
edits.content: If the clue is a bare fragment naming two or more REAL people or things ('Princess A & Princess B', 'Senators X and Y', 'Players P, Q'), answer with the ONE proper noun they all share: the country or realm (princes, princesses, kings, queens), state or city (senators, governors, mayors), team, band or work. A bare '<title> <person name>' (president, king, prime minister + name) likewise asks for the country or state that person led, as a bare place name without the title and not the person's name. Relationship or category words ('sisters', 'royalty', 'family', 'politicians') are never the answer, and neither is one of the listed people. Pick the place or group that every passage pairs with every name.

edits.target: Before the answer tags, briefly quote the matched line.
edits.content: - The archived answer is final even when it is a bare surname or shorter than the natural full name ('| Smith.' gives 'Smith', never 'John Smith'). Never add a first name, title or descriptor that the archive line does not show; Rule 4's name-form defaults apply only when there is no archive answer. A passage that repeats the clue with no answer after it is not a hit.

edits.target: - Put only the bare answer in the answer tags. Do not write a sentence, restate the clue, or add dates, qualifiers or alternatives. Brief reasoning belongs before the tags.
edits.content: - NEVER give two options joined by 'or' / 'and' ('cat or dog'). When passages list several candidates, commit to the one the best sources call primary ('particularly', 'especially', 'usually', or named first and most often) and output only that word.

edits.target: Never cut a part that identifies the person: keep the regnal numeral of a king or of a play's title character ('Richard III', not 'Richard'; 'Henry V').
edits.content: - PERSON NAMES: when there is no archive answer, default to the plain 'First Last' form without middle initials or generation tags ('First M. Last' -> 'First Last'). If the clue itself spells the person's name, use that spelling. Keep an initial only when a verbatim archive answer prints it or the person is conventionally always written with it (Dwight D. Eisenhower). Tie-breaker: this never overrides the knight rule, so keep 'Sir' where the person is conventionally titled.

edits.target: - For nickname clues about a person ('known as "Uncle Walter"'), answer with the real name as it appears in the context (Walter Cronkite), not the nickname. Still apply the person-name rule above.
edits.content: - DIRECTION CHECK for name clues: first decide which half the clue already gives. If it gives the real name and asks for the 'moniker / nickname / alias', answer only the nickname as the passages print it, without repeating the name from the clue. If it asks for 'the last name / first name of ...', answer only that part, not the full name.

edits.target: - Archive lines may also be formatted 'CATEGORY | clue text | answer'. Take the answer that follows the clue, even if the whole context is one short passage.
edits.content: - Other archive layouts to recognise: quiz-dump pages shaped 'Category: X Question: <clue> Answer: Y', and flat flashcard text where the answer is the capitalised word(s) right after the clue's last word, often after a comma. Take Y as the answer. If it is cut off, complete it from other passages that repeat the same fact.

edits.target: The context passages about the topic usually reveal the link.
edits.content: - A fragment that begins with '...' and names an old, alternate or local name of something ('...as the U.S. holiday <old name>') asks for the OTHER name of the same thing. Find passages saying 'originally called / formerly known as / also called <clue name>' and answer with the name they pair it with. Never answer with the clue's own name.

edits.target: - Honor qualifiers when the context offers several names for the same thing: 'Greek god of erotic love' -> 'Eros' (not Roman 'Cupid').
edits.content: - 'This film series / franchise / TV series / book series' asks for the SERIES name, not the single installment the passages happen to discuss. Drop sequel numerals and subtitles and use the base title shared by every installment.

edits.target: answer with the common English name (Conch).
edits.content: - DEFINITION + ETYMOLOGY clues ('From the <language> for "...", it's another way of saying <synonym>'): the answer is the dictionary HEADWORD. Find dictionary-style passages ('Define X', 'X - definition of X') whose entry text repeats the clue's etymology or synonym, and answer with that headword in its basic form.
